Off unless you turn it on. It covers the apps you send through your circumvention tool or a WireGuard configuration. Datapavan still counts their connections. It also covers apps that connect through a proxy, such as a Telegram proxy. While it is off, Now shows the proxy\'s address while the connection is open and for ten minutes after, and the log keeps that the app used a proxy, which kind, when, which known trackers it reached, and facts that name no address, such as whether a password was sent unencrypted. If you choose to log an app on its row or its page, where it connects through a proxy is logged as if this were on. That leaves out a proxy that Datapavan sees is in Android\'s settings or on your local network. A list of where they went can be used against you if someone searches your phone.

It also covers the connections of a circumvention tool that can run beside Datapavan\'s VPN, such as to its servers or bridges. While it is off, Now shows where such a tool connects while each connection is open and for ten minutes after. The log then keeps the time and the bytes, and in full the connections to a known tracker. You can choose to log where one tool connects for itself instead, on its row or its page in Now.

A PAC file is set for the whole phone in Android\'s settings. It names a proxy, or none, for each connection.
This network\'s settings name a proxy: %1$s. Apps that were already running when Datapavan started use it, and so do the apps you left out. Others connect directly.
This network\'s settings give a PAC file. Apps that start inside Datapavan\'s VPN do not use it.
This is Android\'s PAC proxy, which connects for other apps, including apps you left out.
%1$s is a circumvention tool. This is its own connection through a proxy.

If an app does not work with Datapavan\'s VPN, leave it out. It then goes to the internet without Datapavan: Datapavan does not see or record its connections, and it does not go through your circumvention tool. One exception: where Android\'s settings give a PAC file, what the app sends through Android\'s PAC proxy can come back into the VPN, and Datapavan then sees and records it as that proxy\'s. Android no longer tells that app its network is a VPN, but the app may still find that the phone has a VPN interface. While the VPN is on, a change takes a moment, because Datapavan sets up its tunnel again.

If the app carries other apps\' connections, theirs are logged as its own. If you set this app\'s proxy yourself, leave this off. A list of where it went can be used against you if someone searches your phone.
Android counts these apps as one, so this covers each of them: %1$s.
It also covers the parts of this app that Android runs apart from it, in the SDK Runtime.

It does not cover the proxy in Android\'s settings, a proxy on your local network, or Android\'s PAC proxy. But a proxy that a PAC file names, or one set in Android\'s settings by its name rather than its address, may be logged as this app\'s own. It does not cover a circumvention tool that can run beside Datapavan\'s VPN: such a tool has a choice of its own. Nor does it cover the apps you send through your tool or a WireGuard configuration. Those are logged only while \"Log where apps connect through your tool, WireGuard or a proxy\" is on.
